segments.source_text: Aquaculture Stewardship Council
Indicator: Requirement:

The UoC shall, after the determination of the water quality baseline, conduct monitoring of the water quality parameters listed below, following the method outlined in Appendix 8 (8.8)13:
Total Nitrogen (TN); and,
Total Phosphorous (TP); and,
Dissolved Oxygen (DO); and,
Secchi Disk (SD) depth; and,
Chlorophyll-a (Chl-a).

How do I interpret this requirement?
Quarterly monitoring ensures the UoC can capture any seasonal or inter-annual variations in the data collected.
Measurements should be timed to coincide with, or immediately follow, annual turnover events when the waterbody is not permanently stratified (holomictic).
The UoC should calibrate equipment used to measure DO, TN, TP, SD and Chl-a according to the technical specifications of the equipment.
The UoC should conduct measurements of the parameters in-situ.
Samples may be sent for laboratory analysis, however variability with sample maintenance during transit can lead to inconsistent results. This is particularly evident with DO and Chl-a samples.

Evidence of implementation should be maintained, e.g.:
Documentation outlining the sampling plan to conduct quarterly monitoring and that is in accordance with Appendix 8 (8.8).
Quarterly monitoring data has been collected and submitted to the ASC Water Quality Calculator. Data should be submitted at least annually.
13 An exemption applies if the mean of Secchi Disk (SD) depth calculated over any rolling two-year period remains ≥10m.
Document Name ASC Farm Standard - Interpretation Manual Document ID ASC-INT-001 Version 1.0 Page 103 of 511
Aquaculture Stewardship Council

Evidence that quarterly monitoring data has been timed with annual turnover events (where applicable).
That equipment to measure DO, TN, TP, SD and Chl-a has been calibrated according to technical specifications.

Auditors should confirm:
The sampling methodology to conduct quarterly monitoring is in accordance with Appendix 8 (8.8).
The UoC has conducted quarterly monitoring of the water quality parameters and submitted data to the ASC Water Quality Calculator at least annually.
Evidence has been provided demonstrating the UoC has calibrated equipment to measure DO, TN, TP, SD and Chl-a in accordance with the technical specifications.

Useful Resources
Paerl, H.W., Scott, J.T., McCarthy, M.J., Newell, S.E., Gardner, W.S., Havens, K.E., Hoffman, D.K., Wilhelm, S.W. and Wurtsbaugh, W.A., 2016. It takes two to tango: when and where dual nutrient (N & P) reductions are needed to protect lakes and downstream ecosystems. Environmental science & technology, 50(20), pp.10805-10813.
Information on the appropriate use of Secchi Disks can be found here: ‘What is a Secchi disk’, accessed November 22, 2023: https://www.nalms.org/secchidipin/monitoring-methods/the-secchi-disk/what-is-a-secchi-disk/
Example of a method for Chl-a measurements made using ethanol extraction followed by spectrophotometric measurement at wavelengths 665 and 750nm (using accredited methods: EPA method 445.0: Method 445.0 In Vitro Determination of Chlorophyll a and Pheophytin a in Marine and Freshwater Algae by Fluorescence, accessed November 22, 2023: https://cfpub.epa.gov/si/si_public_record_report.cfm?Lab=NERL&dirEntryId=309417
Cost effective example for measuring using in-situ Chl-a using a field spectroflurometer include the FluoroSense handheld fluorometer manufactured by Turner Designs and the YSI handheld meter with EXO1 (#599080) or EXO2 (#599201) sondes.
Hamdhani, H., Eppehimer, D.E., Walker, D. and Bogan, M.T. (2021) Performance of a Handheld Chlorophyll-a Fluorometer: Potential Use for Rapid Algae Monitoring. Water, 13, 1409: https://doi.org/10.3390/w13101409
Kuha, J., Järvinen, M., Salmi, P. and Karjalainen, J. (2020). Calibration of in situ chlorophyll fluorometers for organic matter. Restoration of Eutrophic Lakes, 847, 4377-4387: https://doi.org/10.1007/s10750-019-04086-z
Document Name ASC Farm Standard - Interpretation Manual Document ID ASC-INT-001 Version 1.0 Page 104 of 511
Aquaculture Stewardship Council
Indicator: Requirement:

The UoC shall, based on the monitoring of the water quality parameters, ensure that there is no decline in trophic status compared to the water quality baseline determined, following the method outlined in Appendix 8 (8.8).

The UoC shall, based on the monitoring of the water quality parameters, ensure that there is no upward rate of change >25% over the previous 24 months, for any of the water quality parameters listed below, following the method outlined in Appendix 8 (8.8):
TN; and,
TP; and,
Chl-a; and,
Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD).

The UoC shall implement a nutrient reduction plan when at least one of the following is identified:
TN, TP or Chl-a has increased by ≥5 index points according to Table 2 in Appendix 8 (8.8), compared to the water quality baseline; or,
TN, TP or Chl-a increased by ≥15% over the past 24 months; or,
The distance from the surface to the zone of oxygen depletion or to the zone of anoxia has decreased by ≥25% over the past 24 months; or,
BOD has increased by ≥15% over the past 24 months; or,
≥1 adverse turnover event or ≥1 harmful algal bloom within the past 10 years.

How do I interpret this requirement?
Quarterly monitoring of TN, TP and Chl-a will determine whether there has been a change in the status of the limiting nutrients or a decline in trophic status. BOD will also need to be calculated annually. The calculated data will be compared to the water quality baseline.
Quarterly monitoring data will be submitted to the ASC Water Quality Calculator at least annually. The ASC Water Quality Calculator will determine rates of change in the limiting nutrient(s) and trophic status compared to the baseline.
A decline in trophic status will be determined when the next Trophic Status Index (TSI) breakpoint has been exceeded, in accordance with Table 2 in Appendix 8 (8.8).
Document Name ASC Farm Standard - Interpretation Manual Document ID ASC-INT-001 Version 1.0 Page 105 of 511
Aquaculture Stewardship Council

Exceedance of the next TSI breakpoint will occur when one parameter falls into the next TSI category.
The ASC Water Quality Calculator also determines whether one of the scenarios in Indicator 2.6.13 has occurred based on the quarterly monitoring data.
If one of scenarios has occurred, an action plan needs to be implemented to reduce nutrients released by the site and/or to have improved the efficiency of the feed used.
The action plan should be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time bound.

Evidence of implementation should be maintained, e.g.:
Monitoring data has been submitted annually to the ASC Water Quality Calculator and results have been obtained.
Results will determine the trophic status and status of TN, TP, Chl-a and BOD, in accordance with Indicator 2.6.12. Results will also be compared to the water quality baseline after the first annual submission.
Any upward transitions in trophic status at the compared to the water quality baseline will be determined based on the results from the ASC Water Quality Calculator.
Results from the ASC Water Quality will determine rate of change for TN, TP, Chl-a and BOD compared to the water quality baseline, specifically whether this exceeds 25% over the previous 24 months.
Results from the ASC Water Quality Calculator will be obtained to determine whether one of the scenarios in Indicator 2.6.13 has occurred.
This will be based on the TN, TP, Chl-a and BOD data submitted to the ASC Water Quality Calculator.
It will also be based on submissions of the number of HABs and ATEs to the ASC Water Quality Calculator.
If one of the scenarios has occurred, an action plan will have been documented which will reduce nutrient nutrients released by the site and/or to have improved the efficiency of the feed used.

Auditors should confirm:
The UoC presents evidence demonstrating monitoring data has been submitted annually to the ASC Water Quality Calculator.
